analysis: The supplied changes are documentation only: docs/developer/test.md (head excerpts at lines 2289-3269 covering test instructions) and docs/provider/direct-mode.md (date bump plus a new paragraph at head lines 340-342). No executable code, configuration, key handling, authorization or crypto paths change. The test.md excerpts describe synthetic CPU/GPU test lanes, e.g. prefix tenant partition checks (lines 2752-2773), SSD prefix record encoding (2947-2996), and served-speed build scope (3252-3269). They state that tests do not establish hardware qualification or production readiness, so there is no overclaim of trust. They are consistent with T-041's tenant-partition and at-rest posture: tests assert that records are found only under their tenant, and the documentation adds no new at-rest artifact or weakened control. The direct-mode.md addition says local telemetry records now note that a request came via the local API (not Darkbloom) and whether the Qwen tensor assistant decoded it, and that plans for serving through Darkbloom ignore local records. That reads as a trust-separation improvement: local, self-reported speed data does not steer coordinator-served placement. The code that implements this (DistributedPairTelemetryRecorder and the planner) is outside the supplied evidence, so the behavior is unverified here. The test.md patch excerpt is truncated and earlier hunks (lines 1214-1325 and others) were not supplied as units, so I could not review them. No regression was found in what was provided. One residual question for integration: whether the telemetry origin field is implemented as documented and is not attacker-influenceable by a coordinator consumer.
